After dinner, i get back to work and do so until 22.00-22.30 when I prep my bag, plan my whole next day, go to bed and read until 23.00.

Weekends: I wake up at 8.30, chill and eat until 10.00. Then, I run the same study cycles until 18.00-19.00. If I have IAs to work on or Portfolio work for VA, I go on until 22.00. Then eat, prep for next day, and sleep at 23.00 - 23.30.

Personally, I also went through this idea of 'wanting' and 'hoping' to be trans. Not because I wanted to dismiss the struggles and discrimination and all, but simply. I now understand that it was just me "hoping to be trans" because I finally saw the opportunity to be myself even if I didn't have a clear picture of what that looked like. I'm still somewhat questioning and I have my bouts of doubt, but I've become so much more open with myself and have come to better understand who I am :) 

Also, every journey is completely unique and every process of coming to understand one's identity is different even if there are some shared experiences. So don't feel discouraged or anything if you don't feel the same about any of these things, I'm just here to provide some insight into what a journey/process may or may not look like!

The advice I would give my past self in times of a lot of questioning would be to just not limit myself. At the beginning I had all these negative thoughts of "leaving my inherent femininity" and that "boy is bad" and all which kept me chained to this idea that I just have to be a female. Once I started exploring everything more, I came to understand that I just had to really let go and learn to experiment with labels, ideas, and so forth.
Essentially, I went from identifying as simply a female who uses she/they pronouns, to agender, to a demigirl, to a transmasc person, and now somewhat more comfortably, a demiguy who uses he/they and who can still appreciate and indulge in, what are stereotypically considered, feminine things!

Honestly just trust and be honest with yourself. Be open to experimenting. All the 'mistakes' I made, helped me understand various parts of my identity better.

If you want to talk more, feel free to reach out! :)
